text:
The Ducks have won five straight and Cutter Gauthier has three hat tricks in five games, so nobody in Anaheim wants to hear the next part. The winning streak is about half real. Over those five games Anaheim took 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and scored 26 times on 17.1 expected. For the season the Ducks are at 48% of the chances and nearly 11 goals ahead of what those chances usually produce.

The clearest example is the top line. Mikael Granlund, Gauthier and Beckett Sennecke have outscored teams 5-3 together, but they've given up 4.34 expected goals per 60 and own only 33% of the chances when they're out there. That's a line that lives on finishing, and Gauthier's 17 points in 10 games on 10.6 expected is the kind of run that cools. Tristan Luneau (11 points in 10) is in the same boat. The Ducks also take 5.2 penalties a game, which is a lot of nights spent killing.

Still, 21 points is 21 points. Our simulations put them at 59% to make the playoffs, projecting about 91 points. The Killorn, Judd Caulfield and Leo Carlsson line is the one that's winning its minutes honestly. What we'd watch: whether the top line starts tilting the ice before the shooting comes back to earth, and how much of Jackson LaCombe's 30-minute nights the defense can keep asking for.
